subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — CentraMed
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@centramed.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@centramed.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & bake-off recap from today's call — CentraMed

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Key pain points you shared
- High per-token cost and unpredictable unit economics on your current hosted endpoints.
- Latency spikes during peak hours impacting clinician-facing workflows (95th pct target: <200ms).
- Need deterministic performance for batch reports and synchronous query flows.
- Data security/PII handling: must avoid storing patient identifiers in vendor logs and support customer-managed keys (KMS).

Goals we discussed
- Replace current inference path for clinical summarization and charting with a solution that meets 95th pct latency <200ms and reduces inference cost by ~30%.
- Run a 2-week competitive bake-off to validate latency, throughput, and output quality on your real prompt set.
- Confirm security controls (VPC/private deployment or strict logging controls) for production rollout.

Competitive context / vendors on your list
- Redwood Inference (us): private deployment option, batching/cache controls, transparent per-token cost reporting.
- InferenceCo: claims low latency but unclear on KV cache and prefix caching behavior.
- CloudInfer: strong managed offering but higher TCO for high-throughput workloads.

Proposed bake-off tests (what we'll run)
1) Latency/throughput: 95th/99th percentile latency under realistic concurrency (~100 sessions), steady-state throughput for 8k and 32k contexts.
2) Cost projection: measured tokens-per-request and model-level compute to estimate monthly TCO for your workload.
3) Quality: side-by-side on the same prompt set with your scoring rubric (relevance, hallucination rate, sensitivity to PII).
4) Security & compliance validation: KMS integration test and logging configuration to confirm no persistent PHI in vendor logs.

Next steps (timeline)
- I'll send a bake-off plan and a sample prompt set by EOD today.
- Please confirm the person who'll provide the test dataset + scoring rubric (format: CSV with prompt, expected summary, quality tags).
- Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff for the bake-off next week (June 3–4)? Jordan, what window works for you?

I'll loop Aditya (technical lead) and Lauren (solutions) on the plan for the actual test setup and data ingestion.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa — this captures the conversation well. A few clarifications:

- Data/PII: our legal team requires proof that PHI won't be retained. If Redwood offers a private deployment option, that is preferred. Can you confirm whether the private deployment will avoid third-party logging and support our KMS?
- Scoring rubric: I'll send the rubric and a small sample dataset (50 prompts) by tomorrow morning.
- Timeline: June 3 at 10:00am PT works for a short kickoff. We'll invite our platform engineer (Priya is looping in).

Also: do you have a short vendor comparison table you can share (latency, deployment modes, pricing model) so our procurement folks can see the delta?

Jordan Reyes
